QuestionStmt.S: The formula for the physical quantity is \( P = \frac{x^3 y}{z^2} \) and the percentage error in the determination of physical quantities \( x, y, z \) are 0.6%, 3% and 1.3% respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of \( P \) is

Solution.S:
Given:

P = (x³ × y) / z²

Percentage errors:
• Error in x = 0.6%
• Error in y = 3%
• Error in z = 1.3%

Step 1: Formula for percentage error propagation

For a formula Q = (a^p × b^q) / c^r, the total percentage error in Q is:

Percentage error in Q = |p|(Error in a) + |q|(Error in b) + |r|(Error in c)

Step 2: Apply the values for exponents and errors

Here,
• Power of x is 3
• Power of y is 1
• Power of z is 2 (in denominator, so absolute value taken)

Therefore,

Percentage error in P = 3 × (Error in x) + 1 × (Error in y) + 2 × (Error in z)

Step 3: Substitute the given values

= 3 × 0.6% + 1 × 3% + 2 × 1.3%

= 1.8% + 3% + 2.6%

= 7.4%

Step 4: Final answer

The percentage error in the measurement of P is 7.4%

Thus, the correct option is D (7.4%).
